blocks.content: Quiz: Why do we export a useJournal() hook from JournalContext.jsx instead of just exporting JournalContext directly?
Tap an option below to answer:
It memoizes the context value to prevent re-renders
useJournal() is a plain useContext() call with no memoization logic. Entries and dispatch() still trigger re-renders when updated.
useJournal() is a plain useContext() call with no memoization logic. Entries and dispatch() still trigger re-renders when updated.
useContext() can only be called inside a custom hook
useContext() can be called directly in any function component. There's no such restriction.
useContext() can be called directly in any function component. There's no such restriction.
It creates a separate context copy for each component
Custom hooks don't create separate context instances. All consumers share the same provider value.
Custom hooks don't create separate context instances. All consumers share the same provider value.
It avoids repeating useContext(JournalContext) in every component
Consumers import one thing instead of two. It also lets us add error checking (e.g. null context guard) in one place.
Consumers import one thing instead of two. It also lets us add error checking (e.g. null context guard) in one place.
